title: Crypto fraud complaints - which agency actually has jurisdiction
p1: Lost money in a crypto scam? The first question is usually not 'how do I recover it?' but 'who should I complain to?' Many victims approach the wrong authority and lose valuable time.
p2: A common misconception is that every crypto fraud case goes directly to a single cyber agency. In reality, the right authority depends on how the fraud happened. Crypto scams may involve cybercrime, financial fraud, money laundering, or an unregistered investment scheme.
p3: For online scams, reporting through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal can be a starting point. Banks, exchanges, and law enforcement agencies may also become involved depending on the facts. The key insight: the presence of cryptocurrency does not automatically decide jurisdiction. The nature of the offence does. Quick reporting can improve the chances of tracing transactions and preserving evidence.
conclusion: If someone loses money in a crypto scam, which authority do you think should handle the complaint first: cyber police, financial regulators, or another agency?
